records.english: {SPEAKER:05}Come on, come on. You'll understand when we get there.
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio impatiently urges Raphael to follow him to the docks.
records.source_meaning: Claudio repeats that Raphael should stop worrying and says he will understand once they arrive.
records.localization_note: Keeps Claudio's repeated coaxing and casual promise instead of flattening it into a terse instruction.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}By the way, {MACRO:FI}... what do you think of men of the sea?
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: On the way to the docks, Claudio asks Raphael about his romantic idea of sailors.
records.source_meaning: Claudio changes the subject and asks Raphael what he thinks of men of the sea.
records.localization_note: Preserves the direct question and Claudio's conversational pause without inventing a definition of a true sailor.

records.speaker: Raphael Castor
records.context: Raphael hesitates because Claudio's broad question catches him off guard.
records.source_meaning: Raphael says that he is not sure how to answer when asked what he thinks.
records.localization_note: Avoids the unsafe literal uppercase first-person macro byte while retaining Raphael's uncertainty and trailing hesitation.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}What are you talking about? Prince Henry, Duke Leon... Man, they're seriously cool!

records.source_meaning: Claudio protests, names Prince Henry and Duke Leon, then openly gushes that they are cool.
records.localization_note: Restores Claudio's boyish excitement and the emphatic reaction that the compressed draft lost.

records.english: {SPEAKER:05}The sea really is a man's greatest adventure!
records.speaker: Claudio Manaus
records.context: Claudio sums up his romantic, exuberant view of life at sea.
records.source_meaning: Claudio declares that the sea is the great romance or adventure of a man's life.
records.localization_note: Uses idiomatic adventure language while retaining his emphatic masculine romanticism.
